observations: Torah 179 has only 3 bechina edges covering 6 unique nodes, which consolidate into 2 packages. No independent domain of 3 or more concepts forms beyond the two proposed packages. The two packages identified — Package 1 (הָרָצוֹן: נֶפֶשׁ / רָצוֹן / מַחֲלֹקֶת / רְצוֹנוֹת אֲחֵרִים) and Package 2 (תַּעֲנִית / צְדָקָה) — fully account for all bechina-connected nodes. The remaining 8 eitza-only nodes (שָׁלוֹם, שִׂמְחָה, שָׂשׂוֹן וְשִׂמְחָה, and various states/outcomes) are outcomes and intermediate results of fasting — they belong to the eitza network between and around the packages, not to any new bechina-grounded cluster. Even if the two suggested missing bechina edges (צוֹם = תַּעֲנִית; כָּבוֹד = רָצוֹן for Torah 179) were added, they would slot into existing packages (Package 2 and Package 1 respectively) rather than creating any new conceptual domain. The Torah's architecture is a lean 2-package teaching whose real richness lies in its eitza chains — the practical, step-by-step argument from problem (strife) through remedy (fasting) to resolution (peace and joy).
